Title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in JWT Verifier via Arbitrary Issuer URL Resolution
Analysis:
The `grpc_jwt_issuer_email_domain` function in `src/core/lib/security/credentials/jwt/jwt_verifier.cc` extracts the email domain from the JWT `iss` claim. If `iss` does not contain an `@` character, the verifier treats it as a URL-based issuer and extracts the host from the `iss` value. It then creates an HTTP request using this host to fetch the OpenID configuration at `https://<host>/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Because there is no validation or allowlist checking on the extracted `host` before it is passed to `grpc_core::HttpRequest::Get`, an attacker can provide a JWT with a malicious `iss` claim (e.g. `127.0.0.1` or `attacker.com`), forcing the gRPC server to perform an outbound HTTPS request (Server-Side Request Forgery).

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
An attacker crafts a JWT with the following payload in the claims segment:
```json
{
  "iss": "attacker.com",
  "sub": "some-subject",
  "aud": "expected-audience",
  "exp": 1900000000
}
```
When the gRPC server receives this token and verifies it using `grpc_jwt_verifier_verify`, it parses the claims and resolves the issuer. Since there is no `@` in `attacker.com`, the server treats it as a URL issuer and makes an HTTP GET request to `https://attacker.com/.well-known/openid-configuration`. If `attacker.com` returns a valid OpenID configuration containing a malicious `jwks_uri` (e.g., pointing to another target), the server will make a second HTTP GET request to retrieve the signing keys.
